family.description: Integrator (INT) complex is involved in the small nuclear RNAs (snRNA) U1 and U2 transcription and in their 3'-box-dependent processing. It binds the C-terminal domain (CTD) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and functions as an RNA endonuclease to cleave different classes of RNAs, regulating the transcription of both protein-coding genes and noncoding elements [[cite:PUB00152015],[cite:PUB00153137]]. Integrator also associates with protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) core enzyme to form the INTAC complex [[cite:PUB00152015]] which regulates transcription through dephosphorylation of Pol II CTD. This entry includes the Integrator complex subunit 1 (INTS1) which forms the backbone module of the complex (it consists of four modules: backbone, shoulder, phosphatase and endonuclease) through the association with INTS2 and INTS7 to form a rigid scaffold. The backbone and shoulder modules form a central cruciform scaffold. INTS1 is an all-alpha helical protein with four repetitive helix hairpin domains towards the C-terminal (R1-R4) [[cite:PUB00152015]]. This entry represents a domain found at the N-terminal of INTS1, which interacts with Pol II subunit RPB2 and form interface A [[cite:PUB00153137]].
family.name: Integrator complex subunit 1, RP2B-binding domain
